key_insight: A unanimous multi-LLM consensus workflow can automatically label clearly normal or abnormal radiology reports with very high precision while routing ambiguous cases to manual review.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help researchers build large retrospective cohorts from radiology reports faster and with less expert review, while preserving reliability for uncertain findings.
method: Reviewed 6,718 brain MRI reports from 5,856 patients.
Used two LLM ensembles: proprietary-inclusive and open-source; a report was auto-labeled only if all models agreed.
Reports with disagreement, including WMH-only cases, were marked uncertain and deferred to manual review.
evidence_signal: In a 680-report expert-adjudicated reference set, both ensembles reached 100% precision for automatically assigned normal and abnormal labels, and the uncertain group was enriched for CNS-related ICD-10 diagnoses.
watch_item: High precision came with more deferred cases, so implementation depends on available manual-review capacity and may vary outside brain MRI report settings.
paper_title: Large language model consensus for reliable research cohort construction from radiology reports: a retrospective cohort study
